name: BN6's sound engine
now: MP2K (m4a) as BN6's code runs it, in the engine's own C, plays the title's and the PET screens' songs and sounds: the same as the game byte for byte, frame by frame, for every song and sound checked against the plain ROM in romlab (tools/mp2k_verify.py). BN5's songs play on the same code, BN5's library being BN6's; the Jukebox plays the three games' music players (BN6's, BN5's, BN4's); every BN5 and BN4 song its game starts named for where it plays, its scripts' music commands decoded from its ROM (tools/bn5_songs.py, tools/bn4_songs.py; BN4's in src/emu/bn4_music.h), three of them played in a run where BN5 plays them (docs/multirom/music.md). Its music and its effects silenced apart (settings.ini's music and effects): a hook on BN6's TrkVolPitSet (0x08150E40, located from bn6f's ply_note and MPlayMain) gives a silenced player's tracks no volume, in the core and in the engine's own C alike; proved by the core's sound dumped (silent from the song's start with the music off, the effects alone before it; with both on the same byte for byte as before). Music and effects in ten levels of 3 dB (2 November 2026): the louder the device's gain, the quieter's share of BN6's own volume given by the same hook, worked out from the track's vol, volX, pan, panX, modM and modT as TrkVolPitSet's code does (read with objdump, +0x12 to +0x18), checked in tests/test_emu.c; a run at the defaults the same byte for byte as before.
left: A frame-by-frame differential of a BN5 song against BN5's own engine state (its RAM's places); BN5's 0x07, 0x08, 0x09, 0x11, 0x12, 0x20 and 0x21, which nothing in Team Colonel starts (tools/bn5_songs.py), and BN4's 0x10, 0x11 and 0x20, which nothing in Red Sun starts (tools/bn4_songs.py), named only by a source that knows them. The Arena's and the stands' two cores take no hook (their states are hashed whole on both players' systems), so a NetBattle is heard at the louder of the player's two levels. A quieter one far under the louder (18 dB and more) loses its quietest notes in BN6's 8-bit volumes.
